Enterprises struggle to move AI agents past pilots

By Pat Example

Large companies are running more AI agent pilots than ever, but few have moved them into daily production use, according to a survey of 900 technology executives published this week.

Respondents most often cited unclear ownership, weak data access controls, and difficulty measuring return on investment as the main obstacles to wider deployment. Only about a quarter said they had a formal process for deciding when an agent is ready to go live.

Several executives interviewed for the report said they had started by limiting agents to read-only tasks, adding write access only after several months of monitored use. One chief information officer described the approach as treating each agent like a new hire on probation.

Analysts expect spending on agent platforms to keep rising, though they noted that budgets are increasingly tied to measurable outcomes rather than experiments.
